Abyss

uh-BISS -- from a root meaning 'bottomless'; an abyss has no bottom in sight. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Abyss is a deep and almost bottomless chasm; a vast, immeasurable depth.

The old mining shaft dropped into a black abyss that no flashlight beam could fully illuminate.

Worked Example

A diver descends past the last rays of sunlight into open ocean water so deep that sonar equipment can no longer find the seafloor below.

That vast, bottomless depth stretching out of sight is exactly what an abyss is. Unlike 'pit,' which can be shallow, abyss specifically implies a depth so extreme it feels immeasurable.

How Abyss Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

chasm

chasm: a deep, wide crack or gap in the earth

void

void: an empty, immeasurable space

depths: the deepest, most distant part of something

Antonyms

surface

surface: the outermost, topmost layer of something

shallows

shallows: an area of shallow water or minimal depth

How Strong Is It? — chasm → abyss → void

chasm vs. abyss

chasm vs. abyss: Chasm is a bit more ordinary than abyss -- a chasm can simply be a wide crack in rock, while abyss emphasizes a depth so vast it feels bottomless.

void vs. abyss

void vs. abyss: Void can feel even more absolute than abyss: abyss suggests an extreme physical depth, while void suggests total emptiness with no bottom or edge at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-

prefix — a-: without (Greek)

root — -byss-

root — -byss-: bottom, depth (Greek (byssos))

Put it together

Put it together: Greek byssos meant 'the bottom, the depths.' Combined with a- ('without'), abyss literally means 'without a bottom' -- a depth so extreme it seems to have no floor at all.

Use the root in a new word: abyssal

Use the root in a new word: abyssal: Abyssal fish have adapted to survive the crushing pressure of the deep ocean floor.
